summary: Interpreted the reconfiguration receipt and bounded the stale-membership half of the account. Receipt 182740a6d29f4af9a99cf83c49f2e857 evaluated all five comparisons: after the long run a current-configuration leader added voter F, and in the feature-on run the restarted node processed that new entry so its view became {A,B,C,D,E,F} (holds, index 4), which ends the stale membership, while at the same event the entries at the conflict index still disagreed (violated, witness index 4) and its FSM still held only the minority write (holds, index 4); the feature-off control reflected the same change and stayed consistent (holds, index 10). That matches the source: a configuration entry the node has never seen is processed on AppendEntries regardless of the scan the restart skipped, whereas same-term duplicates at an existing index are skipped before any processing, so the conflicting entry is untouched. The experiment-level interpretation is explained/asserted, the child and parent accounts now state that the stale membership lasts until the next configuration change while the entry and applied divergence is removed only by an installed snapshot, the configuration-update knowledge entry gained this receipt as a direct use, and the limit lists were revised (single harness-issued AddVoter with no removal or demotion, no snapshot install during the long run, harness-arranged lag for the repair, unexercised user Restore and term truncation, in-memory stores with scaled timeouts). Incomplete: the user Restore and term-changing truncation repair paths, and the operational frequency of the fall-behind that triggers the snapshot repair.
